survived.title: `CLAUDEMD_TABLE_DEG` base bound is not the CLAUDE.md hardware table value — p12 replaces p11's mislabel with a new one, and its `limit_audit` reports the base disagreement in the wrong direction
survived.evidence:
p12:96-101 declares the row and asserts what it is:
```
# The 52nd "urdf_hardware" row, VERBATIM from p11:267-268. ... It is NOT the URDF (see
# `limit_audit` in the results) -- it is the CLAUDE.md hardware table, and it is
# wider than the URDF on shoulder and elbow.
CLAUDEMD_TABLE_DEG = {"base": (-90.0, 90.0), "shoulder": (-110.0, 110.0),
                      "elbow": (-70.0, 190.0), "wrist_p": (-110.0, 110.0)}
```
The actual CLAUDE.md hardware table (CLAUDE.md line 1 is `@AGENTS.md`; the only "RoArm M3 Hardware / Joint Specs" table in the repo is AGENTS.md:388-397) says:
`AGENTS.md:392  | 0 | Base rotation | -190 ~ 190 |` — shoulder/elbow/wrist_p at :393-395 do match (-110~110 / -70~190 / -110~110).
I grepped for any other candidate table: `grep -rn "Base rotation" --include=*.md` returns only `AGENTS.md:392`.
The value -90/+90 is not a hardware number anywhere in the repo; it is the v6 *distribution* clip: `sim_scripts/roarm_kinematics.py:30  "base": (-90.0, +90.0),    # v6 [-49, +76]`. Every on-robot JOINT_LIMITS uses a much wider base: `deploy_smolvla.py:72  (-180, 180),   # 0: Base rotation` and `collect_data_manual.py:64  JOINT_LIMITS = [(-190, 190), ...]`.
My independent URDF parse (command run, output quoted) — `python3 -c "import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET, math; ..."`:
```
base_link_to_link1   revolute  lower=-3.141600 rad = -180.000421 deg | upper=+3.141600 rad = +180.000421 deg
link1_to_link2       revolute  lower=-1.570800 rad = -90.000210 deg  | upper=+1.570800 rad = +90.000210 deg
link2_to_link3       revolute  lower=-1.000000 rad = -57.295780 deg  | upper=+2.950000 rad = +169.022550 deg
link3_to_link4       revolute  lower=-1.920000 rad = -110.007897 deg | upper=+1.920000 rad = +110.007897 deg
```
p12's `urdf_limits_deg()` (p12:144-160) reproduces these to the last digit (I executed it: base ±180.00042091829943, shoulder ±90.00021045914971, elbow -57.29577951308232/+169.02254956359286, wrist_p ±110.00789666511805), and `URDF_JOINT_MAP` (p12:90-95) is correct — the URDF names map onto `roarm_kinematics._CHAIN` qi=0..3 (`roarm_kinematics.py:20-23`) and onto the order `p10.clip4` iterates (`p10:375-380`: `for i, name in enumerate(("base","shoulder","elbow","wrist_p"))`), which equals `p12:87 JOINT_ORDER`. So the URDF side of the audit is clean; the defect is confined to the CLAUDE.md literal.
The error propagates into the machine-readable artifact. From `t3w_smoke1_results.json` `limit_audit.claudemd_table_vs_urdf_disagreements`:
```
{"joint": "base", "claudemd_table_deg": [-90.0, 90.0],
 "urdf_true_deg": [-180.00042091829943, 180.00042091829943],
 "claudemd_wider_lo": false, "claudemd_wider_hi": false}
```
With the real CLAUDE.md value (±190) both flags would be `true` (CLAUDE.md is 9.9996 deg WIDER than the URDF on base, not 90.0004 deg narrower). `t3w_prereg.md:78` carries the same wrong value (`| base | −90 … +90 | −90 … +90 | ±180.0° |`) and :83-85 states the row "is in fact the CLAUDE.md hardware table ... and narrower on base (90 vs 180)".
survived.defensible:
NARROWED (documentation/provenance, minor; no numeric, gate, or verdict impact): p12 fixes p11's "urdf_hardware" mislabel for 3 of 4 joints but over-claims on the fourth. `CLAUDEMD_TABLE_DEG` (p12:100) carries base (-90.0, 90.0), which is not the CLAUDE.md hardware table value — the only such table in the repo (AGENTS.md:392, inlined via CLAUDE.md:1 `@AGENTS.md`) says -190 ~ 190, and no historical CLAUDE.md differed (git show 002b590^:CLAUDE.md:271). That ±90 is the v6 distribution clip (roarm_kinematics.py:30, "# v6 [-49, +76]"), identical to `v6_clip`'s base; shoulder/elbow/wrist_p do match the table. The row is therefore a hybrid: three CLAUDE.md-table bounds plus one v6-clip bound. Consequently three assertions are false as written for base: the comment "it is the CLAUDE.md hardware table" (p12:98), the emitted JSON `note` "its values are the CLAUDE.md hardware table" (p12:420-422, present verbatim in t3w_smoke1_results.json), and the prereg prose "is in fact the CLAUDE.md hardware table ... and narrower on base (90 vs 180)" (t3w_prereg.md:83-85) — against the real table, CLAUDE.md is 9.9996 deg WIDER than the URDF on base, not 90.0004 deg narrower. The minimal fix is textual: state that the row is the 52nd literal = CLAUDE.md table on shoulder/elbow/wrist_p and the v6 clip on base, and either rename the row (e.g. `p11_row`) or add a `base_provenance` field.

Explicitly NOT part of the defect: `limit_audit` itself is correct — it audits the row the probe actually simulates against the runtime-parsed URDF, and both `claudemd_wider_*` flags being false on base is the right answer for those inputs (p12:404-412); nothing is computed in the wrong direction. And the bound is inert in every executed configuration: gate R0 pins psi_pos to 317.5141789665032 or aborts (p12:365-368, 764-770), base tracks psi_pos exactly (all 24 smoke cells base = -42.4858210334968), R5's only alternate azimuths are hard-coded and run under `v6_clip` alone (p12:845-850, max |base| = 85), and R4 `release_base` reproduces the v6_clip theta_max exactly (45.9375 / 48.515625) with `elbow@hi` the sole saturating joint — so no fabricated joint-limit failure can occur without editing the source.

survived.title: The 60° threshold's stated justification cites the wrong limit set; on the verdict axis the correct value is 50°, and the gap is verdict-changing

`t3w_prereg.md:141`: "but **only the `v6_clip` label is the verdict** — the other two are attribution."

```
| IK ok (v6 clip) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
```

survived.defensible:
SURVIVES, NARROWED TO MINOR / DOCUMENTATION-ONLY.

Defensible restatement: `t3w_prereg.md:137-138` states "60° is the smallest θ the 52nd coarse list reported infeasible, so it is the smallest value at which this sweep would have contradicted it." That predicate is false. In the 52nd's frozen `reachability_scan` (`claudedocs/runtime_logs/grasp_track/g0b_d420/t3p_sweep1024_plan.json → reachability_scan.rows`, θ list `[0,6,15,29,35,40,45,48,50,55,60,70,80,90]`) the smallest infeasible θ is **48.0 under `v6_clip`** and **55.0 under `urdf_hardware`**. 60 is recoverable only from the abridged 10-point table in `session_20260811_52nd_...md:156-158` *and* only off the hardware row — the row `t3w_prereg.md:141` explicitly declares is not the verdict. So the stated reason does not reproduce the number it justifies, on any axis.

Two corrections to the filed version: the replacement number is **48, not 50** (the filer read the abridged doc table rather than the frozen rows, reproducing the error being alleged); and the citation for r=0.550 is `t3w_prereg.md:58`, not :63.

Downgrade rationale — the two claims that made it "major" do not hold:
- Not verdict-changing. Only the 75° gate reopens option ② (`t3w_prereg.md:132`); both labels below it (:133, :134) leave the 52nd's retirement standing. Shifting the middle threshold changes a printed label, not a decision.
- The concrete failure cannot occur. `p12:383-386` + `p12:763-771` abort the run with exit 3 / `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAIL` unless θ=50 reproduces as infeasible at seed0_S1; `t3w_smoke1_results.json` shows `gate_r0.pass = True` and anchor `theta_max_deg = 45.9375`. Feasibility at a different radius is not falsification of a measurement the 52nd itself scoped to one workspace point (`session_...52nd...md:176-180`). No θ* value can "contradict the 52nd" in the sense the sentence claims.

Recommended remedy (documentation only, no code change): replace the 60° rationale at :137-138 with either (a) the true frozen numbers — "48° is the smallest θ the 52nd measured infeasible under `v6_clip` (55° under the hardware row)" — and re-derive the threshold from them, or (b) an honest materiality statement ("60° is a chosen materiality band; the 52nd made no claim about other radii, so no θ* contradicts it"). Also fix `t3w_prereg.md:102-104`, which calls `{6,29,35,40,45,50,60,70,80,90}` "the 52nd `reachability_scan` θ-list" — the actual list had 14 points; dropping 48 and 55 removes the two true boundary-crossing samples from the R0 gate, so R0 currently checks a 3°-wide bracket it could check exactly (a separate, also-minor observation, not part of this finding).

survived.title: The 12 mm xy marker nudge is an undeclared visual convention that fuses distinct sweep cells: markers land 1.00 mm apart while their rendered radii are 4.5-7.4 mm
survived.evidence: p12:578-583 offsets every marker by 12 mm along the approach azimuth: `pts.append([base[0] + 0.012 * math.cos(ang), base[1] + 0.012 * math.sin(ang), base[2] + layer_dz[name]])`. `grep -n "0.012|nudge|VISUAL"` over p12 and `t3w_prereg.md` shows the only declaration in the artifact is p12:523 `"(+0 / +0.07 / +0.14 m in z, a declared VISUAL offset, not data)"` — the z layering only; the xy nudge appears solely in a source comment (p12:579-580) and in neither `summary_md` nor the prereg. Recomputing the exact rendered points from `t3w_smoke1_results.json` with the current formula (script run) gives, in every one of the three layers: `OVERLAP dist=1.00mm  r=0.25,dpsi=0.0 (rad 6.45mm) vs r=0.275,dpsi=180.0 (rad 4.94mm)` and `OVERLAP dist=1.00mm  r=0.275,dpsi=0.0 (rad 6.83mm) vs r=0.3,dpsi=180.0 (rad 4.52mm)`, `min pairwise dist = 1.000 mm`. On the DEFAULT full grid (`--r_lo 0.100 --r_hi 0.550 --r_step 0.025 --dpsi_step 30`, 20 radii x 12 azimuths) the same computation finds `pairs guaranteed to overlap (<6.0mm apart, min possible radii sum): 66` per layer, all of the form `1.000 mm : r=0.3250 dpsi=0 vs r=0.3500 dpsi=180`. Marker radius is `0.004 + 0.006*frac` (p12:592), i.e. 4-10 mm, so 1 mm-separated markers are fully merged. Also from `t3w_smoke1_results.json`: `distinct psi_pos over cells: {317.5141789665032}` — every sampled object position lies on a single ray, so the entire 2-D appearance of the point cloud is produced by the undeclared nudge.
survived.defensible: SURVIVES, narrowed to a visual-inspection (D341) defect, not a verdict-integrity defect. Restatement: `p12:582-583` displaces every reach marker 12 mm in xy along the approach azimuth (`ang` from `p12:578`). This convention is declared nowhere a reader of the artifacts would look: the RRD's own summary text (`p12:520-524`) declares only the z layering ("+0 / +0.07 / +0.14 m in z, a declared VISUAL offset, not data"), and `t3w_prereg.md` never mentions it — while `t3w_prereg.md:179` affirmatively states "The RRD's decision subject is ... the sampled object positions coloured by theta_max", which the nudge falsifies. (Partial mitigation the original filing omits: the explanatory comment is archived in the run folder at `t3w_smoke1_script.py.txt:554`, so the convention is discoverable from source, just not from the RRD or the prereg.) The geometric consequence is a parameter collision: 2 x 12 mm = 24 mm is 1 mm short of the default `--r_step 0.025`, so the 12-spoke rosettes of adjacent radius shells interpenetrate. On the default grid (20 radii x 12 dpsi = 240 cells/set, confirmed) 66 pairs per layer fall within 6.0 mm — the distance at which even two minimum-size 3 mm grey markers must overlap — distributed as {1.000 mm: 18, 1.779: 2, 2.779: 2, 4.215: 36, 4.517: 4, 4.679: 4}, NOT all at 1.000 mm as filed. Only the 1.000 mm class is demonstrably destructive: on `t3w_smoke1_results.json` I reproduced, in each of the three layers, two pairs at exactly 1.000 mm where the smaller sphere is fully contained in the larger (`contained=True`, e.g. r=0.25/dpsi=0 rad 6.45 mm vs r=0.275/dpsi=180 rad 4.94 mm), i.e. one cell is invisible. Occlusion is by depth and sphere size within a single Points3D batch, not by log order. Blast radius: bounded. `theta*`, the verdict label, and the per-limit-set argmax cell (with exact `r_m`, `dpsi_deg`, `theta_max_deg`) are carried as exact text in `metadata/run` and `events/verdict` and render legibly in `t3w_smoke1_inspection.png`; every cell is exact in `results.json`/`grid.npz`. So no verdict can be misread off the picture, and AGENTS.md:131-132 makes the JSON the authority. The defensible defect is narrower: AGENTS.md:126-127 requires the RRD to contain the actual decision subject, and `t3w_prereg.md:179` promises per-cell object positions, but panel 1 delivers an undeclared 12 mm rosette in which 18 cell pairs per layer are rendered as a single visible marker — so the mandatory D341 visual inspection cannot resolve the second swept axis (dpsi) per cell, which is the entire novelty of this session over the 52nd. Severity: minor-to-moderate, not major.

killed.title: The "the 52nd's 50 deg is OPTIMISTIC" consequence is asserted from a premise about the wrong row, is not a theorem (the two limit sets are not nested), and is contradicted by p12's own smoke run in all 8 measured cells
killed.why_refuted:
REFUTED — the finding's severity rests on a logical inversion, and its key evidence uses a field the code itself documents as invalid for that inference.

(1) INVERSION. The claim attacked is an inequality: t3w_prereg.md:86-87 "the true URDF envelope can **only be <= ** what it reported". I reproduced the smoke comparison (python over t3w_smoke1_results.json): all 8 cells `theta_urdf == theta_claudemd`, `all equal: True | any claudemd > urdf: False`. Equality SATISFIES `<=`. So the 8 cells are a case of the claim, not a counterexample; a refutation needs `theta_urdf > theta_claudemd`, which the auditor's own printout shows occurs nowhere. What is shown is that the caveat is non-binding at these 8 cells (gap 0.000000), not that it is wrong-signed. The CONCRETE FAILURE sentence "The conclusion drawn is the opposite of what was measured" is therefore false: `<=` and `==` are not opposites.

(2) EVIDENCE (a) USES THE WRONG FIELD, AND THE CONCERN IS ALREADY HANDLED. The auditor concludes "the boundary is set by the 3 mm position gate, not by a joint limit (`argmax.claudemd_table.saturated_at_boundary == []`)". p12:297-299 states verbatim: "The largest FEASIBLE theta is by construction not clipped -- what a joint limit does is make the next theta up infeasible. So the attribution has to be read one step ABOVE the boundary, not at it." p12:302 computes `just_over = rows[last_ok + 1]` and p12:322 emits `saturated_just_over` for exactly this attribution. Demonstration that an empty `saturated_at_boundary` proves nothing: I printed `v6_clip` at the anchor radius — `theta_max= 45.9375  saturated_at_boundary= []` — yet the v6 boundary IS elbow-limited: gate_r0 v6 row theta=50 has `sat=['elbow@hi']`, and R4 shows `R4:release_elbow:r0.2898:d0.0 = 50.15625` vs `release_base/shoulder/wrist_p = 45.9375` (baseline 45.9375). So the same empty field coexists with a joint-limited boundary. The auditor is also citing a superseded run: t3w_smoke1_results.json has no `theta_just_over_deg`/`saturated_just_over` keys (KeyError when I indexed them) and `sha256(t3w_smoke1_script.py.txt)=6dc188a21bce0326...` != `sha256(p12)=f8703fa2ee1db16c...`.

(3) THE PREMISE IS NOT "ABOUT THE WRONG ROW" AND IS CONFIRMED BY THE RUN. t3w_prereg.md:85 openly sources it: "Since the **v6** boundary saturates the *elbow upper* and *wrist-pitch lower* bounds". That is verifiably true (gate_r0 v6: `['elbow@hi']` at theta=50, `['elbow@hi','wrist_p@lo']` at theta>=60). The inference — the joint that binds under the tighter clip (elbow@hi) is the one the looser row over-widens (190 vs URDF 169.02) — is confirmed as the causal joint by R4 (release_elbow alone reproduces the whole claudemd gain). What the measurement adds is a magnitude the caveat could not know a priori: the elbow never exceeds 157.97 deg (gate_r0 claudemd theta=90 q=[-42.49, 56.7, 157.97, -110.0]), i.e. never crosses 169.02, so the over-widening is inert. "Causally right, quantitatively inert" is not "premise false for the row in question".

(4) (b) IS DISCLOSED, NOT HIDDEN, AND ITS COUNTEREXAMPLE IS UNREACHABLE. The non-nesting is stated in the same prereg sentence ("and narrower on base (90 vs 180)", t3w_prereg.md:85), and p12:411-412 computes and ships per-joint `claudemd_wider_lo`/`claudemd_wider_hi`, which the JSON reports as false/false for base AND for wrist_p, true/true only for shoulder and elbow — exactly the scope the note's clause "where it is WIDER than the URDF" names. So the code asserts no nesting. The offered counterexample (theta=90 saturating `wrist_p@lo` where URDF is wider) sits on a row with `ok=False` under both boxes; an infeasible theta is not a boundary and cannot raise `theta_max`, and the margin is 0.00790 deg (-110.00789666511805 vs -110.0).

(5) (d) IS SELF-DECLARED UNREALISED AND IS ALREADY PROBED. p12:829-834 builds the R4 ablation by releasing each v6-clipped joint TO THE URDF VALUE (`merged[joint] = sets["urdf_true"][joint]`) with `ablation_sets["release_all"] = sets["urdf_true"]` — i.e. p12 does vary the limit box across 5 additional boxes. All 10 ablation rows are >= the v6 baseline and `nonmonotonic_cells == []`. Ten negative probes, not zero.

(6) THE NOTE CANNOT DRIVE THE DECISION. `limit_audit` is prereg-designated R1 "limit-set audit (report, not gate)"; the verdict comes from `_verdict_for(theta_star)` only; and the same JSON ships `theta_star_deg = {"v6_clip": 48.515625, "claudemd_table": 51.328125, "urdf_true": 51.328125}`, `verdict_per_limit_set` for all three rows, and per-cell `theta_max_deg` for `urdf_true` in the R2 sweep, R3 focus and R4 ablation. The failure story requires quoting a static caveat while ignoring the settling measurement three keys away in the same object.

killed.title: Gate R0's tilt@90 tolerance for `claudemd_table` is 5x looser in code (0.005) than in the preregistration (±0.001), and the already-observed value falls in the gap
killed.why_refuted:
The finding's line citations are all accurate, but its central claim — that the code's looser tolerance lets a real reproduction failure through — is refuted by the frozen baseline. I compared p12's smoke Gate-R0 output against the 52nd's frozen artifact directly:

  cd claudedocs/runtime_logs/grasp_track/g0b_d420 && python3 -c "... compare t3p_sweep1024_plan.json:/reachability_scan/rows (urdf_hardware -> claudemd_table) vs t3w_smoke1_results.json:gate_r0.rows ..."
  -> "compared 20 bit-differences 0"
  -> 52nd hex  0x1.d58ba902bb521p+3 14.673298364005463
  -> p12  hex  0x1.d58ba902bb521p+3 14.673298364005463
  -> abs delta vs 52nd artifact = 0.0
  -> abs delta vs prereg literal 14.67 = 0.003298364005463128
  -> v6 52nd/p12 hex 0x1.592686c11db26p+5 0x1.592686c11db26p+5 delta 0.0

All 20 anchor rows (10 theta x 2 limit sets) match bit-for-bit, including tilt@90 for BOTH rows at delta exactly 0.0 with identical IEEE-754 bit patterns. The reproduction Gate R0 exists to verify is exact.

The 0.003298 "gap" is therefore not a divergence in the probe; it is the transcription precision of the literal at p12:109. "14.67" is the only form in which that number has ever been published: session_20260811_52nd_g0b_t3p_randomized_parallel_sweep.md:164, t3p_prereg.md:121, and START_HERE.md:27 all print it to two decimals. "43.1438" was upgraded to four decimals by reading the frozen JSON. That is exactly why p12:110 carries two different tolerances: 0.005 is the half-ULP of a 2-decimal-rounded literal (the tightest bound a correct reproduction of a 2-dp published value can be held to), and 0.001 is a comparable bound for the 4-dp literal. The tolerances are precision-matched, not arbitrarily loosened.

The reductio: the auditor's proposed "registered" behavior (apply +/-0.001 to both rows) would make Gate R0 abort with ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAIL on a run that reproduces the 52nd baseline BIT-EXACTLY. That is a false-negative gate — the proposed fix is the defect, not the code. The code satisfies its own stated purpose verbatim (p12:28 "solely to reproduce the 52nd row bit-for-bit"; p12:29-31 "reproduces the 52nd reachability_scan anchors exactly").

Two subsidiary claims also fail. (1) "The real agreement is +/-0.0033" is false: agreement with the 52nd baseline is 0.0; +/-0.0033 is agreement with a rounded printout. (2) "Any session write-up would be false" is false: t3w_smoke1_results.json gate_r0.checks records expected 14.67, observed 14.673298364005463, and tol 0.005 verbatim, so full provenance is on disk and nothing is concealed.

Severity is also not defensible as "major": tilt@90 is a diagnostic residual, not a verdict input. The preregistered verdict thresholds are theta* >= 75 / >= 60 deg (t3w_prereg.md:112-118), and the decision-bearing R0 checks are exact equality — max_theta uses `==` (p12:377) and ok_pattern uses tuple equality (p12:386). A ~0.008 deg window on a residual tilt diagnostic cannot move a 60/75 deg verdict boundary.

killed.title: `theta_just_over_deg` / `saturated_just_over` are read at the coarse grid point (up to a full 5° above the ceiling), discarding the tight infeasible bracket end the bisection already computed
killed.why_refuted:
The control flow is quoted correctly (I reproduced the auditor's exact numbers by driving the real `_worker_cell` with a stub `_evaluate`: theta_max=47.1875, theta_just_over=50.0, bisect samples [(47.5,F),(46.25,T),(46.875,T),(47.1875,T),(47.34375,F)]). What fails is the claim that this is a defect — that the discarded tight infeasible bracket end is the better attribution point.

1) The stub begs the question. It hardcodes `saturated_descend=['elbow@hi']` at EVERY infeasible theta, i.e. it assumes the joint clip engages the instant feasibility ends. Real p10 output contradicts this. In `claudedocs/runtime_logs/grasp_track/g0b_d420/t3w_smoke1_results.json`, cell `R2:v6_clip:r0.2898:d0.0` (the seed0_S1 anchor) has `theta_max_deg=45.9375`, `saturated_at_boundary=[]`, and `q_descend_at_boundary` elbow = 133.8123 against its 135.0 clip — 1.19 deg short of saturation. `SAT_TOL_DEG = 1.0e-6` (p12:119) flags a joint only when it is exactly clipped.

2) The proposed fix would be strictly worse on that cell. Real elbow slope near the boundary is 0.9861 deg/deg (from the smoke focus rows: 40 deg -> 127.9572, boundary -> 133.8123). The bisection's tightest infeasible sample lies at boundary+0.15625 deg => elbow ~133.97; even boundary+1 deg => 134.80. Both are below 135-1e-6, so `saturated_just_over` read there would be `[]` — naming no joint at all. The current coarse read at 50.0 deg is exactly where the focus rows show elbow = 135.0000 and sat = ['elbow@hi'] (i.e. the correct single joint). Reading closer to the ceiling empties the diagnostic; reading a coarse step out is what makes it non-empty.

3) The code does not contradict its own comment. p12:297-299 says the attribution must be read "one step ABOVE the boundary, not at it". One coarse step is literally what p12:301-302 takes. The comment never says "the tightest infeasible bisection sample". The asymmetry with p12:295 is purposeful: the feasible side is the measured quantity (theta_max, the verdict number, needs bisection precision) while the infeasible side is a clip-engagement diagnostic (needs margin, not precision).
